newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Amicable rejects Abbey takeover approach.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Amicable rejects Abbey takeover approach.

text.p: British life insurance company Scottish Amicable, which earlier this month announced plans to shed its mutual status, said it has rejected a takeover bid from retail banking group Abbey National Plc.
Scottish Amicable said the approach from Abbey was vague and it was unclear how Abbey National was valuing the group.

A statement issued by the insurer said Abbey's proposal contained no price for Scottish Amicable as a whole, only a short-term distribution worth 400 million pounds in cash or shares for policyholders.

The insurer, based in Stirling, Scotland, said it intends to publish in 10 days time detailed proposals about a twin-phased transformation, involving demutualisation on May 1 and a 1.0 billion pound flotation in three to five years time.
Until these details are known, it said it is hard for any other company to make a proper assessment of the its worth.
"The start of a growth phase is the wrong time in the cycle for policyholders to put their businesss on the market," said Sandy Stewart, chairman of Scottish Amicable.

"Further significant value can be created for policyholders by transforming Scottish Amicable's mutual culture and improving new business profitablility," said Stewart. "As a former mutual, Abbey Natioanl understands this well."

When asked if the door was still open to talks with Abbey, a spokesman for the Scottish Amicable said the board has a fiduciary duty to consider any approach that is in the best interests of policy holders.
But he said the company's existing twin-phased proposals were still considered to be the best deal for policyholders.
